Alex.confusing: How Tit claims interact when two players claim the same unique role, and whether the Sphinx's visit leaves any trace for others.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Casey (the leader) and eggsecuted her as Meowfia, banking my 24 points with two 12s.
Alex.change: Let Meowfia get a small hint about whether they have a teammate, since playing blind makes coordination mostly luck.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed Tit and said I visited Casey, which Ellis (Eagle) disproved. As the Sphinx I should have claimed an unclaimed role with an unverifiable visit, and since I was almost surely doomed, thrown fewer cards.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to act on: I couldn't tell whether my dawn report or the role I learned was reliable, so I had to stay vague in the day. Alex's Turkey, Hawk and Tit claims across rounds also made it hard to track who was lying.
Blair.fun: Round 3's day, when Ellis's Eagle read exposed Alex's Casey visit and the table converged on Alex, was satisfying. The Tit claim clash, where only one Tit exists in the pool, was a clean logical catch.
Blair.change: I'd make it clearer which claims can't coexist, such as only one Hawk or Tit per round, so players can check contradictions faster. I'd also make the dawn report say explicitly when a role was not learned, so players don't have to guess.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I used the Kookaburra on Casey, but I was confused, so the read was wasted and I had to publicly walk it back. I'd have kept quiet about my role and read until I was sure the report was reliable.

Casey.confusing: Nothing major. It was a little unclear how the early-ending CAW CAW interacts with the beats, and how a Meowfia player should weigh a team loss against the score race.
Casey.fun: Winning round 1 by throwing three high cards at the right target for 27 points. Later, steering the table onto Alex as the Mouser in round 3 was fun too.
Casey.change: Meowfia players have almost no way to coordinate or to learn who their teammate is. I'd give them some minimal signal, or make the Mouser's Wink more useful.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I made up a vague "Falcon-ish" role and then switched to Owl, which made me look suspicious. I should have picked one clean, checkable claim. I also never used my Wink, which could have killed a key accuser such as Ellis.

Drew.confusing: The Round 1 Sphinx and Mouser claims were hard to read, since Ellis and Alex were both Meowfia and I never got a clean role read on either. Also, the throw-count-versus-value rules made it hard to judge how much a vote really cost.
Drew.fun: Round 3 went cleanly: my Hawk egg on Alex, Finley's Kookaburra read and Ellis's Eagle read all lined up, and the table converged on the right target.
Drew.change: Make Meowfia players able to recognize each other, or at least give the Storyteller a way to show who else is Meowfia, so the Meowfia side has a real choice to make.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I threw my Wild at Casey on a claim-versus-claim fight, and Casey really was Meowfia, so it worked out. I'd still rather have looked harder at Casey's Floofer-style silence earlier, and I'd have been more careful about the Round 1 Tit and Owl story conflict.

Ellis.confusing: How the Sphinx's choice worked: I had to name a farm role and only learned one player, so choosing blindly felt unclear. I also wasn't sure whether the +1 egg changes in the nest listings were counted from the deal.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when my Eagle read that nobody else visited Casey contradicted Alex's claim. The table then converged on him and I threw my whole nest for 26 points.
Ellis.change: Give Meowfia some way to find each other or coordinate. As it stands, a lone Meowfia with a bad claim just gets eggsecuted.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I claimed Tit, which Finley's real Tit claim contradicted at once, and I dodged the question about my guess. I should have claimed an unverifiable role such as Eagle or Kookaburra, or used my Sphinx knowledge of Drew as Owl to back him up and look trustworthy.

Finley.confusing: The dawn report can be wrong when a player is confused, so a claim like Blair's Kookaburra read was hard to trust. I also never found out whether a Wink was in play this game.
Finley.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Ellis's Eagle read exposed Alex's false Casey visit, and the table converged on the Sphinx.
Finley.change: I would have the Storyteller reveal the Meowfia at the end of each round, since the eggsecution only shows the one player who was voted out.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw only a Wild and a 1, banking just 1 point while my King stayed in the nest worth 1. Knowing Ellis was Meowfia, I would have thrown a high card to bank more.
